parsed.notes:
The heading 'Das bringst du idealerweise mit' contains 'idealerweise' (= ideally, a listed optional marker). On the literal reading the whole section is nice_to_have, and that includes German. This is a conventional German requirements heading, so a person should confirm.
If the heading is read as a requirements heading, these become required: data-engineering, azure, data-factory, sql-db, data-lake-storage, databricks, functions, and German.
These stay nice_to_have either way under the appetite rule ('Interesse an'): azure-ai-foundry, data-warehousing, business-intelligence and cloud.
The Azure examples are given as 'wie z. B. Data Factory, SQL DB, ...' with no 'oder', so I did not treat them as an alternative_group. Groups were not reviewed.
The 'Databricks' and 'Functions' quotes are lengthened to stay unique, because 'Databricks' also appears in the benefits section and 'Functions' would be ambiguous on its own.
I read 'Functions' as azure-functions because it sits in the Azure Data Dienste list.
I did not map 'Leidenschaft für Daten, Azure und AI' or 'AI' as a skill: it is too vague, and passion is not an asked skill.
'Data Lake' as part of 'DWH / Data Lake' is folded into data-warehousing via its alias.
Technologies that appear only in the tasks or benefits sections (LLM integration, agent-based pipelines, Azure Cloud in tasks) are not labeled.
No degree is mentioned.
Seniority is stated in the title.
